samples.summary: `parseMerges` caps per-span cells (100k) and entry count (10k) but nothing caps the product, so a ~250 KB body can still store 1e9 covered cells and make the tab unopenable
samples.evidence: Line 174 rejects a single span over `MaxMergedCells = 100000`; line 141 rejects more than `MaxMergeEntries = 10000` entries. Neither bounds the sum: 10,000 distinct anchors each with `{rs: 100000, cs: 1}` passes both checks (each entry serialises to ~25 bytes, so ~250 KB, far under the 25 MB body limit) yet gives 1e9 total covered cells. `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap()` — the very function both comments cite as the reason for the caps — inserts one Map entry per covered cell on every document load, so such a stored map is exactly the "document nobody can open again" the guard exists to prevent, and it is only recoverable through another API call. The new entry cap therefore does not close the hole its own doc-comment claims to close; a cumulative `sum(rs*cs)` ceiling is what is missing.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: parseMerges bounds only per-entry values — entry count at worksheet-settings.ts:141 (10,000) and a single span at :174 (rs*cs > 100000, so rs:100000/cs:1 is accepted, as spec.ts:106 asserts). Per-entry rs may reach MaxRows-anchor.r+1 (:168) and anchors can occupy 10,000 distinct columns, so 10,000 non-overlapping {rs:100000, cs:1} entries pass every check and yield 1e9 covered cells in a ~250 KB body. No aggregate check exists downstream: PUT /merges (worksheet.controller.ts:226-255) calls only parseMerges (:234) and the per-entry freeze-straddle check assertMergesClearOfFreeze (:184-200) before assigning ws.merges (:249); Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap (sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:851-863) then walks rs*cs per entry and Map.sets one entry per covered cell on every loadMerges (:577-580) with no ceiling, and yorkie-store.ts getMerges (:1010-1018) caps nothing. A repo-wide grep for aggregate ceilings found only per-item caps for this feature (MaxMergedCells, MaxMergeEntries, MaxClearedCells, MaxAxisCoverage, MaxBorderSelectionCells, MaxCheckboxToggleCells); the only cumulative-budget precedent in the repo is MAX_TOTAL_IMAGE_BYTES (miro.service.ts:106), whose comment states the same rationale but which was not applied here. No counterexample found, so the absence claim stands; impact is a stored merge map that makes the tab unopenable for all collaborators, recoverable only through another API call — a broken-invariant/state-corruption defect in the Correctness lane.
